newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban Catholic church creates press association.
newsitem.headline: Cuban Catholic church creates press association.

text.p: Cuba's Roman Catholic church, currently enjoying improved ties with the authorities, has established an association of Catholic journalists, a rare non-official media grouping on the communist-ruled island.
November's edition of the Havana diocese magazine Palabra Nueva, issued on Monday, said Cuban Catholic Press Union had held its first national meeting earlier this month.
The establishment of the group, a branch of the Catholic Union of Latin American Press (UCLAP), comes amid a climate of improved church-state relations.
President Fidel Castro held an historic first meeting last week with Pope John Paul at the Vatican, and it was agreed the pontiff will visit the island next year.

Palabra Nueva, one of several diocese-based Catholic publications in Cuba, said the Cuban branch of UCLAP was approved last June by the Cuban Catholic bishops conference. It did not mention whether the government had given approval for the group.

Reflecting the difficulties of the Cuban church in the past, Palabra Nueva noted that most of the new organisation's members were not journalists by profession, since journalism in Cuba had been barred for a long time to people practicing religion, but rather Catholics who had worked on church publications.
The creation of the new association coincides with recent requests by church authorities for the church to be allowed access to the state media.

Cuban journalists generally work for the state-controlled media and are grouped under the official journalists union UPEC. There are separate associations, such as a group of economic journalists, but these are for the official media.
Since last year there have been some Cuban journalists trying to operate independent press bureaux, but these are illegal and their work is published only abroad.
